title: Observability suppression policy prototype and triage playbook
content:
Status: draft. Purpose: capture an operationally actionable suppression policy + triage steps for the most common noisy observability failures we've seen in the last 3 months: 1) bursty SLO-burn alerts coming from downstream dependency jitter, 2) missing host/agent metrics after node reboots or agent restarts, and 3) cascade alerts amplified by aggressive alerting rules (too-many-high-cardinality groups).

Summary of recent incidents motivating this doc:
- INC-1245 (2024-09-28): multiple SLO burn alerts for api.latency across eu-west region. Root cause: transient disk pressure on a downstream logging cluster causing higher p99 for a subset of request paths. Alerts fired repeatedly because the SLO alert rule evaluated on a 5m window with no suppression and we had noisy path-level cardinality.
- INC-1310 (2024-11-02): ~150 hosts reported missing 'node_exporter:up' within a 10m period during a kernel upgrade wave. The collector process cycled and restarted with new ephemeral hostnames; alerts did not suppress and oncall pagers were noisy.
- INC-1399 (2024-11-30): A deployment increased traffic to a new model route; caching misconfiguration caused KV cache miss spikes and downstream latency; SLO burn alert cascaded into database-pool-exhausted alarms.

Observed failure modes and why they amplify pager noise:
- Missing metrics that are transient (agent restart/upgrade) produce a flurry of "instance down" alerts with little actionable info.
- High-cardinality alert rules (group_by: [path, method, model_id]) will explode when a path-level transient spawns many unique labels.
- SLO alerts fired on short windows without hysteresis or escalation levels (no soft/critical tiers).
- Lack of cross-alert correlation: downstream latency triggers SLO, DB pool alerts, and 500 error rate simultaneously; oncall gets paged multiple times for what is a single root cause.

Proposed suppression policy principles (high level):
1) Detect the "class" of alert (metric-missing vs transient error vs sustained degradation) and apply different suppression behavior.
2) Implement short automatic suppression windows (mute) for metric-missing events triggered by node restarts or agent upgrades, with automatic unmute after a health-check pass.
3) Add score-based alert deduplication: if multiple alerts share the same top-level symptom (eg. p99 latency increase on api.frontend service) within Xm, collapse to a single incident with a summarized pager.
4) Introduce SLO alert staging: warning (soft) -> critical (hard) with different notification channels. Warning goes to slack & dashboard, critical pages oncall.
5) Reduce cardinality in noisy rules by moving to service-level aggregates and surface top-3 offenders to console dashboards rather than pagers.

Concrete runbook (on-call triage steps) - first 15 minutes:
1) Identify the symptom: check the alert summary, Prometheus graph, and the top related alerts (Prometheus groups).
2) Run quick diagnostic queries:
- Are host metrics missing? promql: up{job=\"node_exporter\",instance=~\"eu-west.*\"} == 0
- SLO burn check: 
  (sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"0.5\"}[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) by (service)) < 0.95
  (we keep a plain-text version here for frictionless copy/paste)
- KV cache miss spike: rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m]) / rate(kv_cache_requests_total[1m]) > 0.1
3) If missing-metrics pattern detected and recent automation/deploy exists (check /deployments and recent chef/ansible/argo events), apply temporary mute: create a suppression for the alert group with a 20m timeout and add note: "auto-suppress: rolling host maintenance".
4) If SLO burn present: check for correlated downstream errors (db connection retries, queue depth). Query examples:
- db pool exhaustion: rate(db_connection_errors_total[5m]) > 5
- queue length: sum(queue_depth{queue=~\".*api.*\"}) by (queue) > 200
5) If a single root cause is identified (eg: logging cluster slow), create a single incident in Jira, add a summary, link the relevant alerts, and mark duplicate alert groups as "suppressed" with explanation.
6) If no root cause emerges within 15m, escalate to oncall second with annotated graphs and the last deploy id.

Suggested Prometheus rule changes (examples to land in ops-config):
- Change: api_request_latency_slo_burn to evaluate warning and critical levels:
  - warning: (p99 over 10m) > 0.9 * SLO -> slack only
  - critical: (p99 over 30m) > SLO threshold -> page oncall
- Change: host_down (high-cardinality per-instance rule) -> host_down_agg: if > 5% of instances in a cluster are down for > 2m, alert cluster-level. Single instance downs get logged in dashboard but do not page.
- Add rule: metric-staleness-detector that looks for many 'up==0' events across instances with matching restart_signals and auto-suppresses per-policy while notifying platform-ops channel.

Suppression automation sketch (implementation notes):
- Use alertmanager beehive or our alert router to set dynamic mute windows via API. When detector sees a node-restart pattern it POSTs to /api/suppressions with: {group: cluster-name, reason: \"node-restart-batch\", ttl: 20m, owner: auto-suppress-service}.
- Maintain suppression audit log (linked in incident ticket).
- The suppression service must validate health by checking an associated service health endpoint before unmuting (example: 2 consecutive scraping cycles with up==1).

Metric hygiene checklist (to prevent repeat noise):
- Remove unnecessary labels from high-frequency rules (model_id, session_id) when used for pager conditions. Keep high-cardinality labels for dashboards only.
- Where possible, aggregate by service and surface top-k offending labels in dashboards.
- Add explicit agent-version and rollout metadata to host metrics so we can detect upgrade waves as a suppression signal.

Experiment plan (two-week runway):
Week 1:
- Land 3 rule changes: host_down_agg, SLO warning/critical split, metric-staleness-detector in staging.
- Run suppression automation in dry-run: log actions but do not actually mute. Evaluate false positive suppression risk.
Week 2:
- Enable auto-mute for node-restart signatures with 15m TTL and health-check unmute.
- Monitor missed-action risk: ensure that auto-muted incidents are surfaced to platform-ops slack channel and logged to the incident board.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Auto-suppression hides real outages (eg. a subset of hosts actually down for >15m). Mitigation: health-check gating before unmute and cluster-level thresholds that will still page.
- Risk: Over-suppression of SLO warnings leads to missed early signals. Mitigation: keep soft warnings visible in slack and dashboards and require critical window before paging.

Open questions for engineering/observability review:
- What is an acceptable TTL for node-restart mutes? (15m vs 30m)
- Should we gate auto-suppress only to scheduled deploy time windows or allow during unexpected waves?
- How to best score/deduplicate alerts that are across subsystems (api latency vs db pool) but same root cause?

Action items / owners:
- Jonas: prototype host_down_agg rule and add labels to host metrics (due 2024-12-05).
- Maya: land SLO warning/critical split into staging and create dashboards for top-3 paths (due 2024-12-08).
- Liam: implement dry-run suppression logger in router (due 2024-12-11).
- Priya: coordinate SRE postmortem template update and runbook edits (due 2024-12-12).

Appendix: quick PromQL snippets for oncall copy/paste:
- cluster-level host down ratio:
  sum( (1 - up{job=\"node_exporter\"}) ) by (cluster) / sum(1) by (cluster)
- p99 over 30m: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30m])) by (le, service))
- metric staleness:
  count_over_time(up{job=\"node_exporter\"} == 0[10m]) > 5

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive; we want concrete, testable changes rather than vague guidance. Please comment inline with objections, add implementation links, and mark anything you want to take ownership of.

Recent edits log:
- 2024-10-03 Priya initial draft
- 2024-11-12 Jonas added suppression automation sketch and promql snippets
- 2024-11-30 Maya added experiment timeline and owner assignments
- 2024-12-18 Priya updated risks and moved to 'draft' for wider review

End of document.
